problem_text:
A regional power grid operator must schedule a maintenance tour across ten critical substations.

The travel times between substations, measured in minutes, are as follows:
* Substation Alpha to Beta: 118.6 minutes
* Alpha to Gamma: 49.0 minutes
* Alpha to Delta: 43.2 minutes
* Alpha to Epsilon: 27.9 minutes
* Alpha to Zeta: 131.7 minutes
* Alpha to Eta: 106.3 minutes
* Alpha to Theta: 92.8 minutes
* Alpha to Iota: 81.6 minutes
* Alpha to Kappa: 103.8 minutes
* Beta to Gamma: 82.2 minutes
* Beta to Delta: 95.3 minutes
* Beta to Epsilon: 146.2 minutes
* Beta to Zeta: 40.1 minutes
* Beta to Eta: 48.1 minutes
* Beta to Theta: 88.8 minutes
* Beta to Iota: 47.2 minutes
* Beta to Kappa: 155.7 minutes
* Gamma to Delta: 60.3 minutes
* Gamma to Epsilon: 75.3 minutes
* Gamma to Zeta: 85.6 minutes
* Gamma to Eta: 89.8 minutes
* Gamma to Theta: 98.0 minutes
* Gamma to Iota: 63.0 minutes
* Gamma to Kappa: 136.3 minutes
* Delta to Epsilon: 63.0 minutes
* Delta to Zeta: 120.3 minutes
* Delta to Eta: 69.1 minutes
* Delta to Theta: 49.6 minutes
* Delta to Iota: 49.7 minutes
* Delta to Kappa: 76.4 minutes
* Epsilon to Zeta: 159.3 minutes
* Epsilon to Eta: 130.6 minutes
* Epsilon to Theta: 110.6 minutes
* Epsilon to Iota: 107.4 minutes
* Epsilon to Kappa: 104.0 minutes
* Zeta to Eta: 87.3 minutes
* Zeta to Theta: 125.3 minutes
* Zeta to Iota: 79.4 minutes
* Zeta to Kappa: 188.9 minutes
* Eta to Theta: 43.2 minutes
* Eta to Iota: 27.0 minutes
* Eta to Kappa: 112.4 minutes
* Theta to Iota: 47.3 minutes
* Theta to Kappa: 69.4 minutes
* Iota to Kappa: 109.8 minutes

The objective is to determine the most time-efficient circuit that inspects every substation precisely once and concludes back at the initial facility.
